# Output Filters and Paging

_Extreme Fabric Engine · 9 commands_

Cut long show output down to what you need with a pipe after the command (| include, | exclude, | begin, | count, | head, | tail), plus the column and header options most people never use. Filters work on every show command except show fulltech.

## Details

### `<show command> | include <pattern> [field <n>] [ignore-case] [header <n>]`

```
show running-config | include i-sid
show running-config | include "radius server host"
show running-config | include "^vlan create"
show running-config | include "radius|tacacs|snmp-server host"
show logging file | include error ignore-case
```

The pattern is a regular expression; quote it when it contains spaces. Handy pieces: `^` start of the line, `$` end of the line, `.` any character, `.*` anything, `[0-9]` one digit. Matching is case-sensitive unless you add `ignore-case`. Alternation (`a|b`) is standard regular expression syntax, but no Extreme document shows an example: keep the pattern in quotes and try it once on your release. Keywords can be shortened like any CLI word (`| inc`).


### `<show command> | exclude <pattern> [field <n>] [ignore-case] [header <n>]`

```
show isis adjacencies | exclude UP
show running-config | exclude "^#"
```

The second example drops the comment and section lines of the config, which makes it much shorter to read.


### `<show command> | begin <pattern> [field <n>] [ignore-case] [header <n>]`

```
show running-config | begin "router isis"
show running-config | begin "interface gigabitethernet 1/5" ignore-case
```

Everything after the first match is shown, not only that block. For one feature, `show running-config module <module>` is shorter. The config writes "GigabitEthernet", so add `ignore-case` when you type it in lowercase.


### `<show command> | include <pattern> field <n> header <n>`

```
show vlan basic | include byPort field 3 header 6
show vlan basic | exclude private field 3 header 6
show vlan basic | tail 8 header 6
```

`field` counts the columns separated by spaces, starting at 1, so a pattern can't hit the wrong column (a VLAN named "byPort-test" doesn't match in column 3). `header <n>` prints the first n lines as they are, so the column names stay above the result: count the lines up to and including the column names in the plain output. Works the same with exclude, begin and tail.


### `<show command> | count`

```
show vlan basic | count
show vlan mac-address-entry 100 | count
```

The count includes the title, separator and column-name lines, so subtract them for the number of table rows.


### `<show command> | head [<n>]`

```
show running-config | head 40
show vlan basic | head 9
```


### `<show command> | tail [<n>] [from-line <n>] [header <n>]`

```
show logging file | tail 20
show vlan basic | tail from-line 15 header 6
```


### `<show command> | no-more`

```
show running-config | no-more
```

Like `terminal more disable`, but only for this command. Use it when you copy the output into a file or a ticket.


### `terminal more disable`

```
terminal more disable
terminal length 64
```
